subject: What Changed to Your Credit Card Today? Edition 5
summary: Kotak Mahindra Bank pulled the fuel surcharge waiver off three more cards, the NRI Royale Signature, Royale Signature, and Privy League Signature, continuing the pattern from yesterday's edition.
body_html:
What Changed to Your Credit Card Today?

Edition 5, 23 August 2026

If you read yesterday's edition about Kotak quietly pulling the fuel surcharge waiver off four of its corporate and Solitaire cards, brace yourself: it happened again today, on three more Kotak cards. Two of them aren't even for sale anymore, which is the part that should actually worry you if you're still carrying one. A benefit getting cut on a card you can still apply for is annoying. A benefit getting cut on a card the bank has already discontinued, one you're stuck with until you decide to switch, is a quieter kind of unfair. Nobody's writing you a letter about it. It just showed up as a removed line on the product page.

NRI Royale Signature Credit Card

This one's still active and squarely aimed at NRIs who want to spend in India without the usual currency hassle. The card used to waive 1% of the fuel surcharge on transactions between ₹500 and ₹3,000, capped at ₹3,500 a year. That waiver line is gone now.

Here's the math. Say you're back in India for a few weeks and fuel up ₹2,000 a time, four times a month. At 1%, the waiver saved you ₹20 a fill, about ₹80 a month. Not life-changing on its own, but if you use this as your primary card while you're here and fuel up more often, you could have been getting close to the full ₹3,500 annual cap. That's real money that now just becomes a surcharge line on your statement instead of a waiver.

The catch: the surcharge itself isn't new, every card charges it at the pump. What's new is that Kotak has stopped absorbing it for you on this card. Nobody invented a fee; they just stopped covering one.

Royale Signature Credit Card

This card isn't sold anymore, Kotak discontinued it a while back. If you're one of the people still holding it, this is the change that should get your attention. The waiver here covered a wider bracket than the NRI version, 1% on fuel transactions between ₹500 and ₹5,000, up to ₹3,500 in your card's anniversary year. That line has been removed.

Do the math on a bigger fill-up. Top up ₹4,000 in one go and the old waiver saved you ₹40. Fill up four times a month and that's ₹160 a month, roughly ₹1,900 a year, though the ₹3,500 annual cap means heavy fuel spenders wouldn't have gotten more than that regardless. Either way, that cushion is gone now.

The honest part I want to be clear about: this card is already off Kotak's active lineup, so you can't call up and get the waiver reinstated by threatening to switch cards, there's nothing to switch you to. Your leverage here is genuinely lower than it would be on an active card.

Privy League Signature Credit Card

Also discontinued, also just lost its fuel surcharge waiver. This one had two versions of the benefit depending on whether you're on the free or paid variant: 1% waived on fuel transactions between ₹400 and ₹7,500, capped at ₹4,500 a year on the free variant, or ₹300 a month if you're on the paid variant. Both caps are gone as of today.

If you're on the paid variant and filling up ₹3,000 a couple of times a month, you were getting close to that ₹300 monthly ceiling already, so you were likely capturing most of the value the card offered here. That's roughly ₹3,600 a year, gone. On the free variant with the ₹4,500 annual cap, the loss is smaller per fill but still adds up if you drive regularly.

The catch, same as the other two: this isn't a new charge, it's an old discount disappearing. And because this card is discontinued too, you're not in a position to negotiate your way back to the old terms.

What I'd actually do with this

If you're holding any of these three cards, check your next fuel transaction for a surcharge line you didn't see before. That's the fastest way to confirm the change actually hit your specific card and variant, since Kotak doesn't always publish the exact numbers cleanly for discontinued products.

For the two discontinued cards, Royale Signature and Privy League Signature, this is a good moment to actually compare what you're paying for versus what you'd get on an active Kotak card or a competitor with a similar fee. A discontinued card losing benefits one at a time, with no path to negotiate, is a sign the bank is winding it down quietly rather than all at once. If the annual fee no longer earns its keep once you strip out this waiver, that's worth running the numbers on.

For the NRI Royale Signature, since it's still active, the fix is simpler and free: pay for fuel with UPI instead of the card wherever the pump takes it. Fuel surcharges are a card-network charge, they don't apply to UPI. You'll lose whatever reward points the card earns on that specific spend, but you'll also lose the surcharge that just came back, so it's worth weighing both sides for your own spend pattern before you switch every fill-up over.

The fine print

This is my honest read, not formal financial advice. I'm not your advisor, and before you act on anything tied to your own card, especially a benefit removal like this one, check your bank's official notification and your card's current terms and conditions page directly. But here's exactly how I'd think about it.

Monzy
